c: For A and B, list input pairs 00, 01, 10, 11 exactly once. Each row corresponds to one possible combination.
AND returns 0,0,0,1 for rows 00,01,10,11; only the final row has both inputs high.
OR returns 0,1,1,1; the first row is the only one without a high input.
NOT has one input, so only two rows are required: 0→1 and 1→0.

k.code:

    for B=0 to 1
        if A == 1 AND B == 1 then
            print(1)
        else
            print(0)
        endif
    next B
next A
